Theme

Latin word

cōgitō

cōgitō, cōgitāre, cōgitāvī, cōgitātum

verb, first conjugation

think over, think about (dē + ablative); intend, plan (with an infinitive); think (about), ponder

In this lexicon

  • consider

    also used · classical · Sen. NQ 6.25: dē exitū cōgitāre (Lewis & Short)

  • mean

    also used · classical · Cato, Agr. 1.1: praedium quom parāre cōgitābis

  • think

    the recommended word · classical · Sen. Ep. 63.2: etiam Niobam dē cibō cōgitāsse; Cic. Off. 1.105: mēns discendō alitur et cōgitandō

Examples

  • aedificāre diū cōgitāre oportet, cōnserere cōgitāre nōn oportet, sed facere oportet

    Building you should think about for a long time; planting you shouldn’t think about: you should just do it.Cato, Agr. 3.1

    In the entry for think

  • cum dīxerit etiam Niobam dē cibō cōgitāsse

    since Homer said that even Niobe thought about foodSen. Ep. 63.2

    In the entry for think
